questions.question: What does a fact table primarily record?
options: Measurable events, observations, or states of a business process
Descriptive attributes used to label and group business events
Reference hierarchies organizing products, regions, and dates
Aggregated summaries that replace the atomic rows below them

questions.question: What is the main role of a dimension?
options: Store the numeric measures that analysts sum across a process
Supply descriptive context for filtering, grouping, and labeling
Record one row for each event the source system emits daily
Enforce the uniqueness rule that protects the fact table's grain

questions.question: Why should conversions and visits be stored instead of only conversion rate?
options: Rate columns cannot be stored with decimal precision in a fact
Dimension tables are required to hold at least two numeric keys
Additive components re-aggregate with the correct denominator weight
Averaging the stored rates returns the same result at any grouping level

questions.question: Which measure is normally semi-additive?
options: Order-line quantity sold
Payment transaction amount
Daily page-view count
End-of-day account balance

questions.question: One segment has 1 conversion from 10 visits and another has 50 from 100. What is the combined conversion rate?
options: Approximately 46 percent
Approximately 30 percent
Approximately 60 percent
Approximately 51 percent

questions.question: Why do warehouse dimensions often use surrogate keys?
options: To remove every business identifier from the warehouse model
To let history and multiple sources coexist under one business key
To guarantee that every measure in the fact table stays additive
To keep dimensions free of descriptive attributes and hierarchies

questions.question: What is a table's grain?
options: The physical size of the files the table occupies on disk
The number of partitions the warehouse splits the table into
The exact statement of what one row of the table represents
The count of dimension tables the fact table joins to

questions.question: When should grain be declared?
options: After every dashboard built on the table has been signed off
Once the source data has been aggregated to its reporting level
As soon as the first duplicate row is caught by a build test
Before any dimension or measure is chosen for the table

questions.question: An order has three lines and shipping cost 12 is repeated on each line. What naïve sum results?
Why is atomic grain often valuable?
options: It always occupies less storage than a pre-aggregated table
It preserves the detail that later rolls up into many analyses
It removes the need to join the fact table to any dimension
It makes a declared row key unnecessary for the fact table

questions.question: Ten order lines join directly to three promotions for the same order. How many rows can the join produce?
What is the strongest automated enforcement of a declared order-line grain?
options: A schema comment stating that duplicate lines are unlikely
A row-count chart that is reviewed after each nightly load
A larger warehouse cluster that reruns the load on failure
A uniqueness test on the columns identifying one line

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: What characterizes a star schema?
options: A central fact joins directly to denormalized dimension tables
Every descriptive attribute is stored in its own fact table
No table in the model declares a foreign key to another table
Dimension hierarchies are normalized into further joined tables

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: What characterizes a snowflake dimension?
options: Its attributes are flattened so one hop reaches every label
Its descriptive hierarchies are normalized into extra joined tables
Its rows can never carry an effective-from or effective-to date
Its keys are business identifiers rather than surrogate keys

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: Why can repeated labels in a star dimension cost less storage than expected?
options: Star dimensions are cached in memory, so their labels cost nothing
Repeated labels are held once globally and shared by every table
Columnar compression encodes repeated values very efficiently
Dimension tables are excluded from the warehouse storage billing

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: When is selective snowflaking most justified?
options: When the analytical layer must reach third normal form on paper
When analysts have asked to write more joins in their queries
When each dimension in the model holds only a handful of rows
When a hierarchy is independently governed, reused, or complex

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: Why can normalizing category into a separate table still produce historically wrong reports?
options: An in-place hierarchy edit reclassifies old facts unless versioned
Normalized dimension tables cannot store effective-from timestamps
Fact tables are unable to join through a normalized hierarchy path
Columnar engines ignore foreign keys, so the join returns wrong rows

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: Which evidence should drive the final star-versus-snowflake decision?
options: The diagram with the fewest boxes on the modeling whiteboard
Query patterns, ownership, measured plans, and fanout risk
A standing rule that every warehouse layer must be normalized
The uncompressed size of the source tables before they are loaded
